text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ruthless criminals yesterday attacked a judge and his five year old daughter. "Move heaven and earth to find the culprits", President Glafcos Clerides tells police.
- Diko party leader Spyros Kyprianou sticks to his guns that the justice minister should be replaced.
- Turks open fire on British soldiers on routine maintenance job on the edge of the bases area.
- Effluent dumping from four wineries into the sea causes massive environmental damage in the Limassol area.
- Malta poll could complicate European Union accession plans of Cyprus.
- Privatising state-owned utility companies could boost the operation of the Cyprus Stock Exchange, says the director of a British stockbrokers firm.
- Geneva-based Severis SA financial services receives permission to open a branch office in the International Merchandising Centre opening later this year.
- Trade with Mexico is expected to reach $100 million.
- Diko leader Spyros Kyprianou threatens to withdraw his support from the government unless Justice Minister Alecos Evangelou is replaced.
- Cyprus Telecommunications Authority seeks the power to set its own rates without approval from House of Representatives.
- The National Guard prepares its answers to United Nations proposals on starting a military dialogue with Turkish forces in Cyprus.
